title: PeakPay — Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on PeakPay's need for dedicated GPU capacity for low-latency fraud scoring; discussed isolation (VPC/KMS), burst capacity, autoscaling expectations, and next steps for pricing and a short pilot/benchmark.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account. Jason from our SE team is here to go deep on capacity.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. Quick context — we're PeakPay, payments risk team. We're evaluating options for running our realtime fraud model, currently on-prem inference but hitting some scale limits.
[00:27] Daniel: Daniel from infra — curious about networking and how we isolate data. Marta is on for compliance.
[00:34] Marta: Morning. we'll be focused on encryption, audit trails, KMS, SOC two stuff.
[00:40] Jason: Great, thanks. high level question — what latency and qps are you seeing today and what do you need from dedicated GPUs?
[00:52] Priya: On a busy window we see 400 rps on average, spiking to maybe 1k qps during batch loads. 99th p latency needs to be under 120ms token to token — I know token phrasing is weird, but essentially end-to-end model response under 200ms is ideal for scoring.
[01:12] Sofia: Ok so low latency is a must. Are you currently running any batching or KV cache?
[01:20] Priya: We have a basic cache but it's not model-aware, we want prefix cache / KV cache features. We also would prefer isolation — customer data can't leave our VPC.
[01:31] Jason: Redwood Dedicated supports private deployments with a VPC peering option and customer-managed subnets; you can also bring your KMS. We do SOC2 and can provide audit logs.
[01:45] Marta: When you say bring KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys? We need key custody options and proof of no plaintext exposure.
[01:55] Jason: Yes, HSM/KMS integrations are supported; we can do customer-managed keys. i'll follow up with the exact security pack.
[02:05] Daniel: What about autoscaling — we need predictable throughput but also burst to cloud peaks. how does capacity work with reserved GPUs?
[02:15] Sofia: For Dedicated, customers reserve a pool of GPUs for predictable throughput; we also offer burst capacity to shared host pools for occasional spikes. The policy can be configured — priority to reserved, then burst to hosted, with fallback model variants to lower-cost quantized variants.
[02:31] Priya: How fast is scaling? we can't afford 5 minute cold starts in a payment flow.
[02:36] Jason: Scaling within the reserved pool is immediate; warm workers kept for the pool. Burst to hosted can add a few hundred ms of routing overhead, but we recommend provisioning buffer capacity for tight SLOs. Also, continuous batching and KV cache reduce the need to scale horizontally.
[02:54] Priya: Are there quantized model variants that are functionally equivalent? We need to ensure no accuracy regressions.
[03:02] Jason: We do model profiles and recommended quantization knobs per workload. Redwood Optimize can run evals and alert if quality drifts. For a pilot we can pin a variant and run A/B.
[03:14] Marta: Audit logs — retention options? do logs include token-level data or just metadata?
[03:21] Sofia: Audit logs include request metadata, latencies, and routing decisions. By default we don't store full prompt text unless customer opts in; retention is configurable per plan.
[03:33] Daniel: Networking — is there direct peering? we prefer private links to avoid public internet.
[03:38] Jason: Yep, we support VPC peering and private connectivity. For on-prem we have an appliance option, or you can run Redwood Private in your own cloud account.
[03:48] Priya: Ok, timeline — we want to pilot in 3 weeks, decision in 6–8 weeks. Budget's allocated if the pilot meets latency/cost targets.
[03:58] Sofia: That sounds doable. Next steps would be price estimate, security pack, and a short benchmark plan.
[04:05] Priya: For bench, we can provide sample models — transformer-based scoring model, seq length ~256, batch size low. we'll need your guidance on test harness.
[04:18] Jason: We'll send a recommended harness and a script to drive qps and measure p50/p95/p99. we'll also run a compatibility check to recommend GPU types and quantization.
[04:29] Daniel: Any forced downtime for maintenance on Dedicated?
[04:32] Sofia: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime; maintenance windows are negotiated and we can offer rolling upgrades with minimal impact.
[04:40] Marta: Compliance question — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[04:45] Jason: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for account provisioning. we'll share the integration guide.
[04:52] Priya: Cost — what's the unit economics for reserved vs hosted? we need to justify reserved GPU cost.
[04:58] Sofia: We'll send a pricing sheet. high level: reserved gives predictable per-token costs and better tail latency; hosted is cheaper for low steady-state load but can have higher variability. Redwood Optimize can help model the tradeoffs for your workload.
[05:15] Priya: For our case, predictability and isolation push us to Dedicated, but we'd like a burst strategy to control costs.
[05:22] Jason: Recommend baseline reserved capacity sized for p90 steady-state and burst to hosted for peaks; we can also configure pre-warmed workers for critical routes.
[05:32] Daniel: Any limits on model size or GPU types? we might want to run 70b models or quantized 13b variants.
[05:40] Jason: We support a catalog of open models; Dedicated allows you to bring models or use our curated models. GPU sizing recommendations will depend on seq len and throughput — we'll propose options (A100, H100, etc.).
[05:54] Priya: Does Dedicated support multi-tenant within the pool? we need logical isolation between product lines.
[05:59] Sofia: Yes, within Dedicated you can carve out namespaces and RBAC to limit access; physical isolation comes from reserved pools per account.
[06:10] Priya: What's the expected onboarding time?
[06:13] Sofia: For a pilot using our hosted-backed Dedicated it's about 1–2 weeks to provision and run bench; for full private deployment might be 4–6 weeks depending on networking approvals.
[06:24] Daniel: For benchmarks, can you instrument token-level latency and cost breakdowns?
[06:29] Jason: Absolutely — Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. We'll share an example dashboard screenshot.
[06:40] Marta: One more on data residency — can processing stay in region EU-west? our compliance needs that.
[06:45] Jason: Yes, routing policies can pin region; Dedicated pools can be region-specific.
[06:51] Priya: Ok let's outline next steps and action owners.
[06:55] Sofia: Great.
[07:00] [Wrap-up — recap of next steps]
